subject: environmental-science
title: CFCs and the Antarctic Hole
welcome_lead: 1985 — Farman's Halley Bay measurements stunned the world. Catalytic chlorine had stripped Antarctic ozone.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on CFC catalytic destruction of ozone.
final_note: One chlorine atom can destroy 100 000 ozone molecules — chemistry of catastrophic catalysis.

concepts.def: Chlorofluorocarbons; refrigerants and propellants; long stratospheric lifetime.
Cl + O₃ → ClO + O₂; ClO + O → Cl + O₂; Cl regenerated.
Springtime ozone depletion >50% over Antarctica; reported by Farman 1985.
Ice particles at −78°C providing surfaces for heterogeneous Cl release.
Isolating winter circulation enabling extreme cold and PSC formation.
Relative effectiveness of a substance at destroying ozone (CFC-11 = 1.0).

walkthroughs.body_html: One Cl atom can destroy ~10⁵ O₃ molecules before sequestration. The cycle is closed by Cl + CH₄ → HCl reactions.
British Antarctic Survey detected a 40% spring ozone drop. Satellite data had been auto-flagged as errors.
HCl + ClONO₂ → Cl₂ + HNO₃ on PSC surfaces; sunrise photolyses Cl₂, initiating massive O₃ loss.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: They are the same problem.
Cold winters are caused by warming.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).

mcqs.q: Why is ice-albedo feedback a positive feedback loop?
options: Because warming is positive (a good thing).
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
Less ice means less reflective surface, so more sunlight is absorbed, causing more warming and more melting.

mcqs.q: Why is a cold winter not evidence against climate change?
options: It is evidence - if it gets cold sometimes, warming must be wrong.
Climate refers to long-term averages, not individual weather events.
Cold winters are caused by warming.
Because polar bears help spread heat.
